reviewer: AI reviewer (Claude), not a person; a person should spot-check these verdicts
method: 20 random REQUIRES/TEACHES edges from the graph (throughline.quality.sample_edges, seed 2026). Each judged against the talk's title and abstract: is the concept really required (or taught) as claimed? 'partly' counts as not correct.

edges.evidence: building a skill from scratch
edges.reason: Hands-on sandbox that builds a Copilot CLI skill from scratch.

edges.evidence: use AI not just as a coding assistant
edges.reason: Talk combines Actions with Copilot prompts to automate work; the quoted phrase is generic and agentic workflows are only implied.

edges.evidence: once agents were doing the writing
edges.reason: Case study of the agent-driven delivery pipeline itti built, including where humans stay in the loop.

edges.evidence: connect Copilot activity to metrics your business cares about
edges.reason: Says you'll leave knowing how to connect Copilot activity to business metrics.

edges.evidence: shift left observability means
edges.reason: Observability is the talk's subject rather than a stated prerequisite; assuming basic observability is plausible but not shown.

edges.evidence: shows how a personal productivity hack became org-wide infrastructure
edges.reason: Shows how a shared AI config became an org-wide catalog of MCP servers, skills and agents.

edges.evidence: review of agent contributions
edges.reason: Review of agent contributions is one guardrail in a list; the talk does not teach PR review workflows as such.

edges.evidence: auditable DevSecOps CI/CD pipeline
edges.reason: Shows how GitHub features enable an auditable DevSecOps CI/CD pipeline.

edges.evidence: malicious package in your build can steal the credentials
edges.reason: About stopping malicious packages from stealing CI/CD credentials: core supply chain security.

edges.evidence: remediation becomes a pull request review instead
edges.reason: Autofix turns remediation into a PR review, so the talk reasonably assumes you know PR review.

edges.evidence: use AI and automation to accelerate accessibility
edges.reason: Panel on using AI and automation to accelerate accessibility work.

edges.evidence: coding agents can now write, commit, and deploy code autonomously
edges.reason: Opens by assuming coding agents that write, commit and deploy code; reasonable prerequisite.

edges.evidence: pipelines in GitHub Actions
edges.reason: A migration story that mentions how the team approached Actions pipelines; it would not teach a newcomer Actions workflows.

edges.evidence: agents as the crew
edges.reason: Agent factory talk assumes you know what coding agents are.

edges.evidence: Three squads of AI agents compete on the same codebase
edges.reason: Live match between squads of AI agents; knowing what coding agents are is a fair assumption.

edges.evidence: use the GitHub Copilot CLI to query your knowledge base
edges.reason: Workshop uses the Copilot CLI to query a knowledge base inside real workflows.

edges.evidence: policies and access decisions that shape Copilot management
edges.reason: Workshop on Copilot admin settings, policies, access decisions and reporting.

edges.evidence: Agentic Workflows: Automation at scale
edges.reason: Intro talk titled Agentic Workflows that teaches how to start automating.

edges.evidence: concrete checks to run before you trust the next package
edges.reason: Ends with concrete checks to run before trusting a package, i.e. dependency screening.

edges.evidence: delegation and review
edges.reason: Mentions delegation and review in passing; the talk is about cloud agent infrastructure, not human oversight.
